payload.answer: [hard] Do NOT change the brake. bootstrap.py line 275 reads config['max_cycle_dollars'] correctly and constructs LedgerBudgetSource from it -- enforcement is right, only the DISPLAY is wrong. Confirm that with a test before touching anything, and do not 'fix' the brake to match the display. [hard] One source of truth: after this change there must be exactly one place that resolves a project's caps from config, used by both the brake and the display. The bug exists because there are two readers and only one of them was ever exercised. [hard] Do not invent a new config schema or migrate existing projects to a 'budget' sub-table to make the old code correct -- the top-level key is what `vibey new` writes and what the brake reads; the display should follow it. [hard] A project with no cap configured must display honestly as 'no cap' rather than a fabricated default; printing an invented number is the whole defect. [hard] 100% branch coverage -- this function's cap-reading branch is currently unexercised, which is precisely why it drifted. [hard] Conventional Commits, feature branch into develop.

Fix `vibey cost` reporting budget caps that have nothing to do with the project's actual caps. The command reads config['budget']['max_dollars_per_cycle'] with a hardcoded 40.0 fallback, and config['budget']['max_dollars_total'] with a 250.0 fallback. NOTHING in the codebase ever writes a 'budget' key. `vibey new --max-cycle-dollars 200` writes config['max_cycle_dollars'] at the top level. So the fallbacks fire every time and the command confidently prints 'Cycle Budget Cap: $40.00' for a project configured with $200. Verified live: a project created with --max-cycle-dollars 200 has {'max_cycle_dollars': 200.0} in its config and `vibey cost` reports $40.

Operators deciding whether to grant more budget at a parked budget_exhausted gate. This is the worst possible place for a wrong number: the decision is 'is this run worth more money', and the display is off by 5x in the reassuring direction.

`vibey cost` on a project created with --max-cycle-dollars 200 prints 200. A project with no cap prints 'none' or equivalent rather than 40. A regression test asserts display and brake read the same resolved value from the same helper, so they cannot diverge again. All 7 gates green.

Also mid-run, checking headroom before letting an expensive phase start, and after a run when reconciling what it cost. The gate case is the one that matters, because it is the moment the number changes a decision.

All four -- cycle-only, total-only, both, and none -- and the none case is the important one. A project with no cap configured must display as unbounded, not as a fabricated default. Printing an invented $40 for a project that has no ceiling at all is the defect in its purest form, and it is the state every project created without --max-cycle-dollars is in.

Find them before deciding the fix, because a second reader is how this bug happened. Known: bootstrap.py line 275 constructs LedgerBudgetSource from config['max_cycle_dollars'] and is CORRECT -- it is the enforcement path and must not be changed to match the display. The parked budget_exhausted gate prompt is the other place a cap plausibly reaches a human, and if it renders one it must come from the same resolver. `vibey status` and the TUI dashboard should be checked too. The deliverable is one resolver used by every reader, so display and enforcement cannot diverge again.

Asymmetric, and currently biased toward the expensive error. The display hardcodes $40/$250, so a project configured at $200 reads as though it were near a much lower ceiling. An operator sees '$12 of $40' and grants more, believing they are topping up a small budget, when the real cap is five times that. The failure is not merely a wrong number -- it is a wrong number in the reassuring direction at exactly the moment money is authorised. The opposite error, denying a run with real headroom, wastes the work already paid for.
